Under","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the fold operation is not commutative (e.g., operations with strict sequential dependencies), reordering or duplicating events during replay could yield different results.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If events lack sufficient metadata for the fold to recognize and suppress duplicates, the commutativity argument fails because duplicate effects are not cancelled out.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the event log enforces an ordering that contradicts the commutative assumption, the fold operation cannot disregard insertion order, undermining the claim.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Under this view, the event log itself is merely an ordered sequence of facts; correctness under at-least-once delivery depends on the consumer's fold operation being commutative (or more precisely, idempotent with respect to duplicate events). The writer's only obligation is to append entries; the system tolerates duplicates because folding a set of events yields the same result regardless of insertion order or multiplicity, provided the fold operation suppresses duplicate effects (e.g., via deduplication keys or monotonic updates). The causal chain: writer appends event \u2192 log stores duplicate \u2192 consumer folds stream with duplicate-aware commutative operation \u2192 final state is invariant under reordering and duplication. This reframes the requirement from a property of the write operation (safety/idempotence) to a property of the read/aggregate operation (commutativity/idempotence of the fold).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
